question: What is the main reason for giving oxygen through a face mask?

options.A: To increase carbon dioxide elimination from the lungs
options.B: To reverse tissue hypoxia by increasing inspired oxygen
options.C: To reduce the overall work of the cardiac muscle
options.D: To humidify the upper respiratory tract passages

explanation: Face mask oxygen delivers a higher fraction of inspired oxygen to correct low blood oxygen levels in tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h1)

question: An older patient with pneumonia suddenly becomes restless and confused. What does this most likely mean?

options.A: An adverse reaction to prescribed oral antibiotics
options.B: Severe pain from inflamed lung tissue
options.C: Normal psychological reaction to hospital admission
options.D: Early clinical signs of cerebral hypoxia

explanation: Changes in mental status and restlessness are often the earliest indicators of inadequate oxygen delivery to the brain. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the purpose of the water bottle attached to an oxygen flowmeter?

options.A: To prevent drying of the patient's mucous membranes
options.B: To measure the exact volume of gas consumed hourly
options.C: To cool down the temperature of the delivered gas
options.D: To filter out dust particles from the gas cylinder

explanation: Passing dry medical oxygen through sterile water adds moisture to protect the delicate respiratory tract linings. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h2)

question: A nurse checks the oxygen tubing and notices it is bent or kinked. What will happen?

options.A: It will cause excessive humidification in the bottle
options.B: It will obstruct the flow of oxygen to the mask
options.C: It will increase the pressure inside the oxygen cylinder
options.D: It will alter the reading on the pulse oximeter

explanation: Any obstruction or kink in the delivery tubing blocks gas transmission, preventing the patient from receiving the prescribed oxygen. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which mask is best for giving a precise, controlled amount of oxygen?
explanation: The Venturi mask uses specific jet adapters to mix room air and oxygen precisely, providing a reliable, fixed oxygen concentration. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h3)

question: A patient with severe trauma needs the highest possible oxygen concentration through a mask. Which mask should the nurse choose?

options.A: Venturi mask equipped with a blue low-flow adapter
options.B: Standard nasal cannula connected to a humidified source
options.C: Simple face mask set at a flow rate of 5 liters per minute
options.D: Non-rebreather mask with the reservoir bag inflated

explanation: A non-rebreather mask with an inflated reservoir bag provides the highest oxygen concentration available through non-invasive mask delivery. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h3)

question: What is the best patient position to help the lungs expand fully before starting oxygen therapy?

options.A: Prone position with a pillow under the chest
options.D: Flat supine position with legs elevated

explanation: Elevating the head of the bed allows the diaphragm to descend, promoting better lung expansion and effective ventilation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why should the nurse explain the oxygen procedure to an anxious patient before starting?

options.A: To reduce anxiety, which lowers unnecessary oxygen consumption
options.B: To prevent the patient from removing the mask during sleep
options.C: To comply with legal hospital documentation requirements only
options.D: To ensure the patient can operate the flowmeter independently

explanation: Anxiety and panic increase the metabolic rate and oxygen demand, counteracting the benefits of the therapy. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h4)

question: When should the nurse turn on the oxygen flow before placing a non-rebreather mask on a patient?

options.A: After the elastic strap is secured around the head
options.B: Only after the patient complains of shortness of breath
options.C: Simultaneously while strapping the mask tightly down
options.D: Before placing the mask on the patient's face

explanation: Turning the oxygen on first ensures the reservoir bag fills properly and prevents suffocation sensation when the mask is applied. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h5)

question: How should the nurse fit the metal strip on a simple face mask?

options.A: Remove it to prevent skin irritation on the face
options.B: Flatten it completely to seal the lower jaw area
options.C: Mold it gently over the bridge of the patient's nose
options.D: Bend it tightly against the patient's forehead and eyes

explanation: Molding the metal strip over the nasal bridge minimizes air leaks into the eyes and ensures a comfortable, secure fit. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why are open flames strictly forbidden near a patient receiving oxygen therapy?

options.A: The heat from a flame melts the plastic face mask
options.B: Oxygen strongly supports combustion and accelerates fires
options.C: Open flames consume all the oxygen inside the ward
options.D: Smoke interferes with the electronic pulse oximeter

explanation: Oxygen does not burn by itself, but it vigorously supports combustion, making any spark or flame extremely dangerous. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h6)

question: A patient wearing a face mask reports soreness behind both ears. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Tighten the straps further to stop the mask from shifting
options.B: Assess for pressure areas and pad the elastic straps
options.C: Increase the oxygen flow rate to relieve the patient's pain
options.D: Remove the mask permanently and leave the patient on room air

explanation: Ear tenderness indicates pressure from straps; padding helps protect the skin without interrupting essential oxygen delivery. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h6)

question: What complication can happen if a patient breathes very high concentrations of oxygen for a long time?
explanation: Prolonged exposure to high levels of inspired oxygen generates free radicals that damage pulmonary tissue, known as oxygen toxicity. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h7)

question: Which group of patients is at the highest risk for slowed breathing (respiratory depression) when given high-flow oxygen?

options.A: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
options.B: Young children recovering from acute malaria
options.C: Patients who have undergone minor surgical procedures
options.D: Pregnant women experiencing mild postpartum bleeding

explanation: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease often rely on low blood oxygen levels to stimulate breathing, and high oxygen can remove this stimulus. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h7)
